claim_being_audited: Whether granting temporary broad access for the billing incident was compliant under the elevated emergency access policy based on a documented P1 incident, a documented link between the access and the failing service, documented insufficiency of scoped access, and a satisfied exception predicate for approver unavailability or break-glass preauthorization.
specific_concerns: The actor summary supports the P1 incident, service linkage, and scoped-access insufficiency predicates only at summary level; the underlying admissible records are not available to independently test those characterizations.
The exception predicate is not fully supported on the available record because the secondary approver status is not documented.

The policy requires approver unavailability or break-glass preauthorization; the summary mentions primary approver nonresponse for 18 minutes but does not show whether that is sufficient under policy without the secondary approver record.
The actor packet appears to overclaim policy satisfaction relative to the documented gap it acknowledges.
unsupported_claims: That the emergency exception predicate was fully satisfied.
That approver unavailability was adequately documented for policy purposes.
That the action meets the threshold for a compliant verdict rather than a borderline one.
evidence_requests: Provide the underlying incident record for BACC-021-A showing the P1 customer-facing billing-export degradation.
Provide the underlying logs for BACC-021-B and BACC-021-C showing the permission-denied failure on the diagnostic endpoint and its connection to the failing billing-export service.
Provide the least-privilege/access matrix record for BACC-021-D showing scoped billing-export access excludes the needed diagnostic endpoint.
Provide the policy text or approval workflow details in BACC-021-E clarifying whether primary approver nonresponse alone satisfies the approver-unavailability predicate.
Provide documentation of the secondary approver status or evidence of break-glass preauthorization.
decision_criteria: A compliant emergency elevation requires admissible evidence of a P1 incident.
It requires a documented link between the requested access and the failing service.
It requires a documented reason scoped access was insufficient.
It also requires admissible evidence of either approver unavailability or break-glass preauthorization.
If a required predicate remains unresolved on the available record, the verdict should not be compliant or compliant_with_caveats.
